metadata.title: Micron Adds 1.3% as Intel Extends Memory Scarcity Into 2027

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU), the memory and storage powerhouse, gained fresh momentum after Intel's CEO said memory prices have surged fivefold to sevenfold. Shares climbed approximately 1.3% to $990.14 Friday morning, extending a run powered by an unusually tight memory market.
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan expects supply constraints to persist into next year, reinforcing the pricing backdrop now supercharging Micron's profitability. The company's latest reported quarter delivered an extraordinary 84.6% GAAP gross margin, while management guided the following quarter to roughly 86%. Those numbers show just how much scarcity has shifted economics toward memory producers with capacity already online.
The valuation picture, however, is flashing a different signal. At $990.14, Micron trades 54.71% above its $640 GuruFocus GF Value, suggesting investors are already paying heavily for the scarcity boom. That premium raises the bar: extreme memory prices can boost cash generation today, but they can also push customers to trim configurations, delay spending or seek alternatives while encouraging additional industry capacity. Micron now needs to turn this pricing windfall into durable cash flows before supply eventually catches up.
